The death toll in Bogo was expected to rise. Workers were trying to transport a backhoe to hasten search and rescue efforts in a cluster of shanties in a mountain village hit by a landslide and boulders, he said.

data.text:
CSAFP’S CORNER | Professional Systems, Professional Soldiers: The Roadmaps Behind Today’s AFP

In his latest column, Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff General Romeo Brawner Jr. underscores that the AFP’s professionalism today is no accident—it is the product of years of discipline, planning, and commitment to systems that outlast personalities.

At the core of this transformation is the AFP Transformation Roadmap (AFPTR), aligned with AmBisyon Natin 2040. The roadmap set clear goals, tied strategies to budgets and promotions, and required commanders to be accountable for results. As General Brawner stressed, “Professional arms require professional systems.”

Each major service pursued its own long-term vision. The Army advanced through its Transformation Roadmap, the Navy steered with its Strategic Sail Plan, and the Air Force charted its course through Flight Plan 2040. All of these were anchored on the Performance Governance System (PGS), a framework that demanded both external validation and internalization of governance principles. This ensured continuity and accountability across commands, where, as General Brawner emphasized, “commanders come and go; scorecards stay.”

Equally vital was the participation of civil society through the AFP’s Multi-Sector Governance Council and Advisory Boards. Partners from academe, business, faith groups, and other sectors provided oversight and guidance, ensuring that reforms were implemented with transparency and credibility.

The message is clear: professional soldiers are built on professional systems. By setting standards, holding itself accountable, and embracing public trust, the AFP continues to prove itself as a pillar of democracy—steadfast in crises, transparent in progress, and unwavering in its mandate to protect the nation.
